A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Geometrically Constrained Outlier Synthesis (GCOS). All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCOS experiments on near-OOD classification, CIFAR benchmarks and object detection, alongside conformal-inference results, ablations and repeated-seed evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds computational timing measurements and an ImageNet-100 comparison with VOS in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The PCA-based synthesis, quantile shell, regularization losses and Algorithms 1–3 are retained. The added backbone and default-setting disclosures, rationale for the existing shell percentiles, and ResNet-34 evaluation do not establish a change to the GCOS method.

E1.justification: Appendix G extends image-classification OOD coverage to ImageNet-100, evaluated against iNaturalist, SUN, Places and Textures. ImageNet-100, iNaturalist and SUN are new evaluated datasets; Places and Textures already appear in CIFAR evaluations. Existing near-OOD, CIFAR and object-detection coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new ImageNet-100 experiment compares GCOS with the existing VOS method using ResNet-34; it does not introduce a new comparison method. Updated citation years do not change baseline identities.

E3.justification: The added ImageNet-100 experiment fine-tunes GCOS and VOS for 10 epochs from the same ImageNet-1K-pretrained ResNet-34 and uses energy scoring. A new timing protocol measures fixed synthetic-feature configurations across 10–1000 classes. Existing experiment settings are not revised; identifying WRN-40-2 for earlier experiments is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: New Appendix G analyzes computational scaling by measuring PCA, shell-calibration and synthesis costs across class counts. Existing loss ablations and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses remain unchanged, including v1 Table 10 becoming v2 Table 12. The new calibration-size explanation is discussion, without an accompanying calibration-size experiment.

E5.justification: The new timing benchmark explicitly averages measurements over 100 iterations, adding repeated-measurement information. These are timing repetitions, not additional training seeds. Existing five-seed classification statistics and three-run object-detection reporting are unchanged; the ImageNet-100 results add no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing performance and ablation values are retained. New Table 11 reports ImageNet-100 mean AUROC of 94.3 for GCOS versus 94.1 for VOS, and mean FPR95 of 27.6 versus 28.4, with GCOS worse on Textures. New Table 10 reports component timings, including synthesis increasing from 35.8 to 3845.3 ms across 10–1000 classes.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the exchangeability discussion and the conformal risk-control construction are retained. Moving conformal inference from Section 6 to Appendix D does not alter its mathematics. The new percentile rationale and empirical scaling discussion introduce no proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: geometric outlier synthesis, nonconformity-based regularization and exploratory conformal inference. The new conclusion summarizes the existing near-OOD and feature-space efficiency claims without materially changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 proposes coarse p-values from small calibration sets as a plausible explanation for poor conformal-inference results on Stanford Dogs and MVTec. It also explicitly acknowledges ASH's stronger CIFAR-100 Textures AUROC and Free Energy/VOS advantages on Places365. These refine the interpretation of retained results; the calibration-size mechanism remains untested.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies WRN-40-2 with 128-dimensional features, approximately 600 calibration samples per Colored MNIST class, and defaults including queue size 1000, 10 outliers per class, two directions and 15 binary-search steps. Appendix G identifies the RTX 6000 Ada timing hardware. These disclosures do not establish retuning of existing experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds a limited positioning refinement by explicitly identifying settings where already-cited ASH, Free Energy and VOS outperform GCOS. The distinct cited-work set is otherwise retained; publication metadata updates and the duplicated NPOS reference do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The former Section 6 moves to Appendix D, while a conclusion and impact statement are added to the main text. Appendix G and several explanatory paragraphs are added, with corresponding cross-reference and bibliography updates. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds timing and ImageNet-100 Tables 10–11, moves Table 2 into the appendix, and renumbers the existing ablation table as Table 12. Figures 1–4 retain their content and design. Other changes mainly concern placement and text reflow within the existing two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Appendix G makes earlier scalability claims more assessable through timing measurements and a controlled ImageNet-100 comparison. Added implementation disclosures and explicit far-OOD qualifications improve reproducibility and interpretive balance. The gains are limited: the calibration-size explanation is untested, and Table 10's per-batch timing label is ambiguous beside the statement that PCA and calibration costs are amortized across an epoch.
